verdict.rationale: Better Auth documents built-in OAuth/OIDC capabilities: social OAuth providers, an SSO plugin supporting OIDC and OAuth2 providers, an MCP plugin that acts as an OAuth authorization server, and an RFC 8628 Device Authorization Grant plugin. Community users also report it acting as an OIDC/SSO provider, so developers avoid hand-rolling the protocol. However, none of the evidence names the authorization code + PKCE flow or OAuth refresh-token handling; the session refresh docs cover Better Auth's own sessions, not OAuth tokens. Missing for 10: explicit authorization-code-with-PKCE documentation, OAuth refresh token issuance/rotation documentation, independent hands-on corroboration of these specific flows.

support.subject: As a developer, I can implement standard OAuth 2.0 / OIDC flows (authorization code with PKCE, refresh tokens) without hand-rolling protocol details

citations.quote: This plugin supports OpenID Connect (OIDC), OAuth2 providers, and SAML 2.0.
Better Auth supports multiple social providers, including Google, GitHub, Apple, Discord, and more.
The **MCP** plugin lets your app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource for [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) clients.
The Device Authorization plugin implements the code issuance and approval flow from the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant
